## Selected Quantitative Research Capabilities

::: {.cv-what}
- **Equity signals and portfolio construction:** built characteristic-based and latent-factor models for U.S. stock-return prediction and tested them in rolling out-of-sample portfolios; traced how regularisation and signal-library choices change holdings and returns under transaction-cost scenarios.
- **Python tools:** wrote `naipca`, a Python toolkit for IPCA-family factor estimation with a companion diagnostics package, used for rolling monthly model fits; helped build the Python research and backtesting framework of the Imperial Student Investment Fund.
:::


::: {.cv-what}
- **Forecast evaluation:** built a workflow that compares forecasting models on the same forecast origins, tests whether differences in forecast accuracy are statistically significant (Diebold–Mariano) and shows how far a model ranking depends on the evaluation window and output version (archived UK services-inflation example, 3- and 6-month horizons, pseudo-out-of-sample design with look-ahead documented).
:::


## Research Fields

::: {.cv-plain}
Empirical asset pricing (cross-sectional return prediction, characteristic-based factor models); machine learning and big data in finance (regularised and latent-factor estimators on large characteristic panels); financial econometrics (identification and inference in high-dimensional factor models); portfolio choice and risk management.
:::

## Research

### Working Papers

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions](/research/characteristic-libraries.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[Copying one theme or rescaling themes (theme balancing) adds no information, yet on 153 U.S. characteristics both shift attribution and holdings in four tuned ridge-type procedures; balancing makes same-date target weights differ by 19–28% of average gross exposure. Payoffs depend on method, costs and missing-return valuation. Monthly ridge's 39-to-153 expansion has small, imprecise predictive effects.]{.cv-sum}

[[PDF](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Libraries_and_Portfolio_Decisions_SSRN_v2.pdf){aria-label="Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions, PDF"}]{.cv-plinks}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models: Identification and Inference](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[SSRN preprint, September 2026. DOI: [10.2139/ssrn.7445120](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7445120)]{.cv-pmeta}

[Factor models with identical fit can credit returns differently to latent factors, observed factors and an intercept; fit cannot choose the split, but the inner product chosen for characteristic space does. The paper derives rotation-invariant inference that carries the Gram metric's estimation error, and drift-robust confidence intervals near an intercept cap (exposure budget).]{.cv-sum}

[[PDF](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Space_Metrics_Main.pdf){aria-label="Characteristic-Space Metrics, main paper, PDF"} · [Online supplement](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Space_Metrics_Online_Supplement.pdf){aria-label="Characteristic-Space Metrics, online supplement, PDF"} · [SSRN](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7445120){aria-label="Characteristic-Space Metrics on SSRN"}]{.cv-plinks}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[A Geometric Framework for Identification in Characteristic-Based Factor Models](/research/geometric-framework.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[SSRN preprint, March 2026 (preliminary version). DOI: [10.2139/ssrn.7013178](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7013178). Grows out of the PhD thesis; its inference theory is developed further in *Characteristic-Space Metrics*.]{.cv-pmeta}

[Using a metric taken from the long-run cross-sectional distribution of firm characteristics, the paper derives NA-IPCA, which nests IPCA, caps how much the intercept may carry and admits rotation-invariant inference. In the headline calibrated simulation, NA-IPCA recovers the latent pricing span and an intercept-free IPCA benchmark does not; that design does not isolate the metric.]{.cv-sum}

[[PDF](/assets/pdfs/Geometric_Framework_SSRN_7013178.pdf){aria-label="A Geometric Framework for Identification, PDF"} · [SSRN](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7013178){aria-label="A Geometric Framework for Identification on SSRN"}]{.cv-plinks}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice](/research/characteristic-geometry.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[On 132 U.S. characteristics, Euclidean and Gram-metric IPCA make nearly identical forecasts but different portfolios: a fixed factor-covariance ridge penalises exposures differently; removing only that ridge shrinks the largest relative weight gap to about 0.01%. In one NA-IPCA fit, using the intercept raises the gross Sharpe ratio; the mean-return gain since October 2007 is imprecise.]{.cv-sum}

[[PDF](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Geometry_and_Portfolio_Choice.pdf){aria-label="Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice, PDF"} · [Slides (PDF)](/assets/pdfs/Characteristic_Geometry_and_Portfolio_Choice_Slides.pdf){aria-label="Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice, slides, PDF"}]{.cv-plinks}
:::

::: {.cv-paper}
[[Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors: Evidence from Characteristic-Based Return Forecasts](/research/interpreting-pricing-errors.html)]{.cv-ptitle}

[Working paper, September 2026]{.cv-pmeta}

[What does a smaller estimated pricing error (alpha) tell a model user? On 153 U.S. characteristics, crossing the expected-return estimates and factor spaces of one model's equal- and value-weighted fits shows that their gap in fitted intercept magnitudes mainly reflects different estimated means; residual diagnostics add little to forecast selection (exploratory evidence).]{.cv-sum}

[[PDF](/assets/pdfs/Interpreting_Estimated_Pricing_Errors.pdf){aria-label="Interpreting Estimated Pricing Errors, PDF"}]{.cv-plinks}
:::

### PhD Thesis

::: {.cv-paper}
[*No-Arbitrage IPCA: A Framework for Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing*]{.cv-ptitle}

[PhD thesis, Imperial College London; degree conferred August 2026. Thesis available on request.]{.cv-pmeta}

[Extends IPCA, via the empirical characteristic metric, to nested QZ-IPCA and NA-IPCA models separating latent, observable (Fama–French five factors plus momentum) and residual-pricing components under an intercept cap; gives identification results, an asymptotic linear expansion and projected alternating least squares; simulations and a Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen U.S. panel show near-identical fit coexisting with different identified pricing directions.]{.cv-sum}
:::

[Host: [Prof. Robert Kosowski](https://profiles.imperial.ac.uk/r.kosowski), Co-Director of the Centre]{.cv-sub}

[Research agenda for the visit: economically constrained machine learning for cross-sectional asset pricing and systematic investment.]{.cv-sub}

- Machine learning and high-dimensional data: extending the No-Arbitrage IPCA framework of the thesis to regime-switching factor models in which risk premia vary with macro conditions; combining penalised estimation with economically constrained representation learning to separate alpha signals that survive those constraints from spurious signals driven by weak factors or data snooping.
- Research and practice: using the quantitative platform of the [Imperial Student Investment Fund](https://ibconnect.imperial.ac.uk/sif/home/) to test research signals as implementable strategies, net of transaction costs and within turnover and risk limits.

## Research Experience

:::: {.cv-row}
::: {.cv-when}
Aug 2019–Aug 2026
:::
::: {.cv-what}
**Doctoral research**, Department of Finance, Imperial College London (asset pricing, financial econometrics, machine learning in finance)

- Models and geometry: characteristic-based factor models with an explicit characteristic-space geometry, using the empirical Gram metric of firm characteristics as the identification convention; the extension of IPCA to the nested QZ-IPCA and NA-IPCA models developed in the thesis.
- Identification and inference: rotation-invariant identification (loading classes modulo latent rotations); asymptotic linear representations that carry the metric's estimation error into standard errors; drift-robust confidence intervals near an intercept cap (exposure budget); projected alternating least-squares estimation; geometry-calibrated Monte Carlo designs.
- Portfolio experiments and trading costs: rolling out-of-sample portfolios (120-month windows, U.S. stocks 1973–2024) that trace weight gaps across metrics to a fixed factor-covariance ridge; information-preserving library interventions (exact copies, theme balancing) across four tuned ridge-type procedures, traced to theme attribution, stock-level ledgers and returns under transaction-cost scenarios; a separate 39-to-153 characteristic expansion of monthly ridge evaluated for stock-return prediction; forecast-evaluation designs that cross expected-return estimates with factor spaces.
- Data and tools: the Jensen–Kelly–Pedersen library of 153 U.S. stock characteristics ([jkpfactors.com](https://jkpfactors.com/); WRDS `contrib.global_factor`, built from CRSP/Compustat), 1962–2025, with point-in-time formation alignment; a CRSP/Compustat panel built following the Kelly–Pruitt–Su replication dataset (36 characteristics plus a constant, 12,813 firms, 1964–2014); CRSP daily dollar volume for trading-capacity checks; NBER recession dates. Author of `naipca`, a Python toolkit implementing IPCA, QZ-IPCA and NA-IPCA with a companion metric-diagnostics package (available to academic users on request).
:::
